newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX COB electric futures settle lower, PV higher.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX COB electric futures settle lower, PV higher.

text.p: NYMEX California-Oregon Border (COB) electricity futures settled lower Tuesday, but Palo Verde (PV) futures finished higher amid a retrenchment in natural gas futures.
"The news is that electricity did not follow gas," said a New York futures broker.
NYMEX February Henry Hub natural gas futures settled down 30.2 cents at $3.334 per million British thermal units (mmBtu) after falling as low as $3.280 on profit-taking from Monday's sharp rise.
February gas deliveries to the San Juan/Blanco Hub in New Mexico finished near $3.05-$3.10/mmBtu from $3.50-$3.55 earlier today.

Less influenced by the gas futures activity, COB and PV futures took cue from the spot cash market. Daily power prices in the Northwest were pressured by ample hydroelectric supplies while those in the Southwest were bolstered by heating demand due to colder-than-normal weather, market sources said.
February COB settled down 38 cents at $14.87 a megawatt hour (MWh) after trading between $14.40 and $15.00. March COB ended up five cents at $13.85 near its session high of $13.90.
February PV settled up 15 cents at $17.13/MWh after hitting a session low of $16.40. March PV ended down 10 cents at $15.80, trimming a 50 cent loss.
Separately, heavy winds in the Los Angeles area caused scattered power outages, with about 50,000 Southern California Edison Co customers without power as of midday Tuesday.
NYMEX COB and PV electricity volumes for Tuesday were not available.
